runs.rejection_summary: Researched three candidates against the static baseline profile. Two accepted: Carter (81) and Sisu (65), both dense and varied with a capable lead. Warrior was rejected at 52 - the martial arts are excellent but arrive in short bursts, and the period presentation plus heavy drama emphasis pull it under the 60 minimum; that is a verdict about this profile, not about the show. No candidate tripped the action_density hard exclusion this run. Personalization is dormant: no personalized-scores.json exists and none was created. Zero duplicates against the identity set.

Fight or Flight cleared the minimum on recurring close-quarters combat and stunt-heavy action after its setup; Heads of State cleared comfortably on varied action, pursuit structure, spectacle, conspiracy and ensemble charisma. No candidate tripped the action_density hard exclusion or any combination guardrail. Personalization remains dormant because data/personalized-scores.json is absent. Zero duplicates against the public identity set and watched-exclusion set.

Researched two current movie candidates against the static baseline profile. Accepted The Furious (73): multiple whole-runtime sources establish action_density 9, with the action beginning within minutes and leaving barely a quiet stretch thereafter; its varied martial-arts styles, stunt work and brutal close combat clear the 60 minimum without firing a guardrail. Mutiny was rejected because the whole-runtime evidence conflicts too sharply to establish action_density responsibly: one review describes evenly distributed action, while another describes slow pacing, dull exposition and only occasional bursts of intense action. Under the Action contract, uncertain density is not accepted. No hard-exclusion or below-threshold rejection was asserted for Mutiny because density was not responsibly measurable. Personalization remains dormant because data/personalized-scores.json is absent. The mandatory fresh final duplicate re-check found zero duplicates against the current public identity set and watched-exclusion set.

Neither candidate triggered the action_density hard exclusion or any combination guardrail, and neither fell below the 60 minimum. No density, guardrail or below-threshold rejections this run. Personalization remains dormant because data/personalized-scores.json is absent. The mandatory fresh final duplicate re-check found zero duplicates against the current public identity set and watched-exclusion set.

Researched two current movie candidates against the static baseline profile and accepted both: Nobody 2 (66) and Normal (61). Whole-runtime evidence established action_density 7 for Nobody 2: despite a mid-film lull, its lean runtime repeatedly returns to improvised brawls, firearms and stunt-heavy set pieces. Normal is action_density 5, deliberately not inflated by its marketing: a substantive review reports roughly 40 minutes with no action before the bank-robbery conspiracy turns the back half into sustained gunfire and violent escalation; its mystery/conspiracy structure carries the deterministic score just over the 60 minimum. Neither title triggers the action_density hard exclusion or a combination guardrail, and neither falls below the 60 minimum. No density, guardrail or below-threshold rejections this run. Personalization remains dormant because data/personalized-scores.json is absent. The mandatory fresh final duplicate re-check found zero duplicates against the current public identity set and watched-exclusion set.

Researched four current movie candidates against the static baseline profile. Accepted The Running Man (78) and Predator: Badlands (70). Whole-runtime evidence established action_density 6 for both: The Running Man's pursuit/game structure produces frequent action across 133 minutes, while Predator: Badlands opens with roughly 20–30 minutes of near-continuous action and remains an action-heavy sci-fi adventure after that initial barrage. Neither accepted title triggered a hard exclusion or combination guardrail. Mercy was rejected by the defining action-density hard exclusion: its 99-minute structure is overwhelmingly a seated AI trial, with the protagonist strapped to a chair for the central premise, so physical action occupies too little of the runtime. One Battle After Another was also rejected on density: at 161 minutes, a whole-runtime review explicitly places most of its action in the final act, keeping action_density at or below the hard-exclusion line. Personalization remains dormant because data/personalized-scores.json is absent. The absolute pre-write duplicate lock freshly re-read data/library.json and every current discovery file and found zero duplicates; exact backup searches for tt14107334 and tt31227572 also found no existing public identity, and neither candidate appears in watched baseline evidence.

Researched two current movie candidates against the static baseline profile. Accepted Mayday (62): whole-runtime evidence supports action_density 6, with recurring fights, aerial danger, vehicle pursuit and stunts across its 112-minute Cold War buddy-action structure; it clears the 60 minimum and triggers no hard exclusion or combination guardrail. Apex was rejected below threshold at 53 despite action_density 6: its 95-minute survival chase does not fire the density hard exclusion, but its narrow action modes, repetitive cat-and-mouse structure and limited concept/mystery support leave the deterministic baseline score below 60. No density or guardrail rejections this run. Personalization remains dormant because data/personalized-scores.json is absent. The absolute pre-write duplicate lock freshly re-read data/library.json and every current discovery file and found zero duplicates; an independent exact repository search for tt28014327 also found no existing public identity, and the candidate is not watched baseline evidence.

Researched two current movie candidates against the static baseline profile and accepted none. Alpha (2026) was rejected because whole-runtime evidence conflicts too sharply to establish action_density responsibly across its long runtime: some coverage describes excessive or relentless action, while other substantive review coverage describes a sluggish, dull first half and limited pulse. Onslaught (2026) was rejected because the strongest whole-runtime review evidence explicitly describes the 92-minute film as notably unhurried and spending substantial time on atmosphere and character setup; the available material does not support assigning a qualifying action_density without guessing. Under the Action contract, uncertain density is rejected before DNA scoring, so no match_score was invented for either title. No accepted candidates survived to the final write gate, therefore no discovery file was created. Personalization remains dormant because data/personalized-scores.json is absent. The final state refresh re-read data/library.json, data/rejections.json and every current discovery file; with an empty survivor list, duplicates remained zero.

Researched two movie candidates against the static baseline profile. Accepted Boy Kills World (78): whole-runtime evidence supports action_density 8, with frequent elaborate stunt-fight sequences and nonstop graphic hand-to-hand and weapons-based combat across its 111-minute runtime; its high-concept dystopian revenge setup, martial arts and splatter-comedy clear the 60 minimum without firing a hard exclusion or combination guardrail. Runner (2026, tt31349844) was rejected below threshold at 58: whole-runtime evidence shows a slow opening with very little action before the cartel pursuit escalates, so action_density was kept at 5 rather than inflated by its later car chases and hand-to-hand combat; it does not hit the density hard exclusion, but the completed deterministic DNA score stays below 60. Personalization remains dormant because data/personalized-scores.json is absent. The final state refresh re-read data/library.json, data/rejections.json and every current discovery file; Boy Kills World passed canonical duplicate and watched-baseline checks.

Researched two movie candidates against the static baseline profile and accepted both: John Wick: Chapter 4 (84) and Extraction 2 (75). Whole-runtime evidence established action_density 8 and 9 respectively: Chapter 4 devotes the overwhelming majority of its 169-minute runtime to extended gun-fu, blades, car combat and stunt set pieces, while Extraction 2 chains an extended prison-and-train escape into a Vienna assault and final close-quarters showdown, with multiple sources describing it as almost all action. Neither title triggers the action-density hard exclusion or any combination guardrail, and both clear the 60 minimum. Personalization remains dormant because data/personalized-scores.json is absent. The final state refresh re-read data/library.json, data/rejections.json and every current discovery file; both candidates passed canonical duplicate and watched-baseline checks. Automatic pre-validation duplicate repair removed Extraction 2 (tt12263384) because its public identity already exists; this supersedes any earlier duplicate-count statement for this run.

Researched two movie candidates against the static baseline profile.
